title: High-content screening of mitochondrial polarization in neural cells derived from human pluripotent stem cells
protocol: Coat a black wall, clear F-bottom 96- or 384-well plate with Geltrex at a 1:100 dilution.
Use transparent clear bottom microplates essential for this assay.
Check which microplates are calibrated with correct dimensions in the instrument.
Consider using other coating reagents such as Matrigel (200 μg/mL) or poly-l-ornithine plus laminin according to surface type.
Split cells using 0.5 mL Accutase for 6-well plates for 5 min at room temperature (RT) (20°C–25°C).
Dilute the Accutase by adding at least double amount of culture media.
Transfer the cells into a 15 mL falcon tube.
Centrifuge for 3 min at 120 × g, remove the supernatant, and resuspend the cells in culture media.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer or cell counter.
Pipette 100 μL cell suspension containing 30,000–50,000 cells per well of a 96-well plate.
Place the plate in a tissue culture incubator for 24 h.
Stain iPSC-derived neural cells with tetramethylrhodamine methyl ester (TMRM) to detect changes in ΔΨm.
Incubate the cells with TMRM at a concentration below 30 nM to avoid dye quenching.
Monitor the accumulation of TMRM within mitochondria to assess mitochondrial membrane potential.
Stain iPSC-derived NPCs with 10 nM TMRM for 30 minutes.
Wash the stained cells before imaging.
For imaging experiments exceeding 30 minutes, dilute TMRM by adding more media to each well without washing out the dye.
Do not use TMRM if there are indications that the plasma membrane potential is changing during the experimental set-up.
Prepare a stock solution of TMRM at a concentration of 25 mM in DMSO.
Protect the TMRM solution from light and store it sealed at -20°C.
Prepare further dilutions in media fresh before each experiment.
Add 10 nM TMRM and 1 μg/mL Hoechst 33342 dye to the culture media.
For control wells, add 10 nM TMRM, 1 μg/mL Hoechst 33342 dye, 10 μM FCCP, and 10 μM antimycin A to the culture media.
Dissolve FCCP and antimycin A in DMSO as 25 mM stock solutions.
Adjust concentrations of FCCP and antimycin A depending on the neural cell type used if necessary.
Mix rotenone with DMSO to inhibit mitochondrial complex I.
Mix oligomycin with DMSO to increase ΔΨm and prevent ATP synthase reversal.
Mix cyclosporine A with DMSO to mitigate mPTP opening.
Include DMSO controls accordingly.
For high-throughput compound screenings, add compounds to iPSC-derived neural cells prior to staining.
Incubate the drugs for 1–24 h depending on the respective compounds.
Add 2 × TMRM and Hoechst (in medium) directly to the cells without aspirating old medium to obtain a final TMRM concentration of 10 nM and 1 μg/mL Hoechst 33342.

Incubate the iPSC-derived neural cells with 50 μL live-cell staining solution for 96-well plates and 30 μL for 384-well plates (with and without ΔΨm modulators) and incubate for 30 min at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Turn on the HCS imaging platform and set temperature to 37°C and CO2 level to 5% if available; otherwise, ensure media contains an alternative pH buffer like HEPES.
Remove live-cell staining solution after incubation time.
Gently wash cells 1–2 times with pre-warmed (RT) PBS without MgCl2/CaCl2.
Add 100 μL for 96-well plates and 30 μL for 384-well plates of phenol red-free cell culture media appropriate for the cell type.
Place the plate in the HCS imaging platform.
Define the plate type (e.g., 96- or 384-well plate based on step 1.a).
Check manufacturer comments on plate usage.
Select the appropriate light source and filter: for instance, detection at wavelength ranges from 365–465 nm for Hoechst 33342 and 550–610 nm for Alexa Fluor 568 / TMRM.
Choose operational mode non-confocal (wide-field fluorescence).
Select the objective.
Determine microscope settings, exposure time, and Z-set-off for additional Z-positions.
Select binning of 2 × 2 to reduce noise and image size and increase acquisition speed.
Choose a well containing iPSC-derived neural cells and take a snapshot.
Find focus height using the Z-stack.
Start at negative values and go up to positive until cells are in focus.
Set the appropriate focus height for each channel individually.
Evaluate brightness and set exposure times for each channel individually.
Set up image acquisition based on a well containing control cells.
Check settings in wells treated with ΔΨm modulators to cover dynamic range and avoid signal saturation.
Choose a different well to confirm or adjust imaging settings and exclude plate tilting effects.
Ensure the plate is correctly placed in the holder.
Define the plate layout.
Select scan area and number of fields needed for each well.
Start the run.
Fill outer rows and columns with buffer solution or PBS to avoid edge effects.
HCS analysis of the mitochondrial membrane potential using open-source software (CellProfiler).
Determine the image processing time based on computer capacity and number of images to be processed.
Acquire 4-8 images per well for robust data generation.
Use Operetta CLS to generate 16-bit images with a pixel resolution of 2160 × 2160.
Process imaging data, which amounts to approximately 8-10 GB per 96-well plate (no outer row image acquisition).
Install CellProfiler.
Download the analysis pipeline (CellProfiler-Pipeline_MMP_20×.cpproj) and pipelines for illumination correction from GitHub.
Open the “CorrectIlluminationCalculate” pipeline in CellProfiler.
Add images to be analyzed by dragging and dropping them into CellProfiler.
Go to “Metadata” in CellProfiler.
Enter the extraction method and metadata source.
Click on the magnifying glass to set an expression that enables CellProfiler to interpret metadata from a file name or folder.
Adjust the regular expression (“Regex”) for metadata interpretation.
Click “Submit”.
Click "Update" to extract and display metadata in the CellProfiler window.
Go to "NamesAndTypes".
Type a name to assign to the images.
Go to "CorrectIlluminationCalculate".
Select the input name based on the name given in “NamesAndTypes”.
Name the output image (e.g., IllumNameOfTheExperiment).
Adjust the smoothing filter size if necessary.
In the example pipeline, set the filter method to ‘automatic’.
If automatic setting does not lead to sufficient illumination correction, try the method ‘Object size’ and enter the approximate diameter of a typical object in pixels.
Use "start test mode" to step through the pipeline and visually check the outcome.
Increase or decrease the diameter if necessary based on visual inspection results.
Go to “SaveImages”.
Select the image to save from “CorrectIlluminationCalculate”.
Enter the single file name for saving.
Define the output file location.
Click "Start Test Mode" to check for errors in the pipeline.
Errors are marked with a red "x".
Click "Analyze Images" to start pre-processing of images using the "CorrectIlluminationCalculate" module.
Click “Start Test Mode” to check for errors in the pipeline.
Click “Analyze Images” to start pre-processing images with the “CorrectIlluminationApply” module.
Save generated images in the defined file location.
Repeat steps 30–37 using the “ApplyIllumCalculate_TMRM” pipeline.
Create and apply illumination functions separately for each set of imaging or sample preparation conditions.
For small image sets, integrate workflow for creating and applying illumination correction into CellProfiler analysis pipeline.
For large image sets, first create and save illumination functions using one CellProfiler pipeline.
Retrieve and apply saved illumination functions using the CellProfiler analysis pipeline.
Open the CellProfiler analysis pipeline for ΔΨm analysis.
Add pre-processed images or raw images generated in step 37 by dragging and dropping them into CellProfiler.
Enter extraction method and metadata source as specified under step 25.
Adjust settings in “NameAndTypes” module of CellProfiler.
Set channel 1 as DNA (Hoechst staining for nuclei) and channel 2 as TMRM (TMRM staining for ΔΨm).
Set default input and output folders in preferences.
Select a filename for saving the analysis results.
Enter a name at “filename prefix” under the “ExportToSpreadsheet” module.
Click on “Start Test Mode” to test and adjust the pipeline.
Specify “Columbus Export (Index and Images)” in the export settings.
Select data and measurements to be exported.
Specify “Export Path” for the selected data.
Start the export from Harmony by clicking “Start”.
Open Columbus software and move to the “Import” screen.
Download the connection file when prompted by the “Columbus Helper Required” window.
Connect the Columbus Helper App with the downloaded connection file.
Install the Columbus Helper App if it is not already installed, following the provided instructions.
Specify the “Import Type: Operetta IDX/TIF” in the import settings.
Specify “Source Folder” for importing data.
Start the import to Columbus by clicking “Start”.
Alternatively, use the “Columbus Transfer” function to automate data migration with a network connection between Columbus and the Operetta CLS system.
Open Columbus software and move to the “Image Analysis” screen.
Select the measurement you want to analyze from the Data Tree on the left.
Choose one single image (e.g., well and field) as representative for analysis.
Load existing image analysis pipeline for ΔΨm quantification by clicking “Load Analysis from Disk”.
Choose File and open the ∗.aas file analysis script file for ΔΨm quantification.
Click "Open" and "OK".
Adjust and test the settings.
Define the final readout parameters of the analysis in the last building block “Define Results”.
Adjust the filters and input parameters of the building blocks to optimize the segmentation of objects.
Select a few other image fields to test and optimize the analysis with these images.
Save the analysis to the database or the file system as an *.aas file.
Start Analysis.
Move to “Batch Analysis” screen.
Select one or multiple measurements in the Data Tree (right click “Select”).
Click "..." to load the saved analysis script file.
Select the analysis script directly from the database in the Data Tree via left mouse click.
Click the green arrow to start the batch analysis.
View the progress of the analysis on the Job Status screen.
Ensure that the used channels for the selected measurements and channel names correspond to those defined in the analysis.
Move to “Export” screen.
Connect to Columbus Helper.
Select your measurement from the Data Tree.
Specify export options.
Choose a destination export folder on your server.
Tick the type of file for the export (for results choose “Results” as *.txt File).
Click the green arrow to start the export.
Find the results as a Text Document in the previously defined folder.
